practiceNotes: Retrieval practice should maintain definitions, representations, assumptions, diagnostic distinctions and method selection; it does not certify proof-writing, programming, laboratory technique or field competence.
Assess extended work separately using unseen problems, reproducible code, laboratory notebooks, raw data, uncertainty analysis, oral defense and revision after feedback.

Laboratory and field projects require suitable facilities, training, supervision and local risk assessment. Use nonpathogenic organisms, low-energy apparatus and safer chemical substitutions where possible.

Human-participant work, identifiable biological data, animal research, genetic interventions and environmental sampling require applicable consent, ethics review and permissions; these are not assumed available.
Security exercises require explicit authorization and isolated systems. Public datasets and synthetic environments can replace unavailable production infrastructure.
Provided scientific software may be used only where a contract says to use it; implementation and proof outcomes require the learner's own algorithmic work.
Clinical interpretation, hazardous synthesis, radiation handling and regulated professional practice are not authorized by completing these decks.

includes: Arithmetic, algebra, functions, units, coordinate geometry and complex numbers

Use Cartesian and polar coordinates, similarity, areas and volumes; calculate with two- and three-dimensional vectors, dot and cross products, and rectangular or polar complex numbers.

practice: Build and check a unit-consistent scaling model from measurements; solve a coordinate-geometry problem using both diagrams and algebra.

Parse text and tabular files, validate inputs, transform records and produce documented outputs while handling errors.
Design boundary and example tests, inspect execution state, isolate defects and explain program behavior.

practice: Implement a command-line data-cleaning application with documented functions, malformed-input handling and automated tests.

decks.description: Infer population-health patterns and evaluate interventions.

outcomes.description: Calculate incidence, prevalence, risk and odds ratios; compare cohort, case-control and trial evidence using explicit confounding, selection and measurement-bias diagrams.

Construct a spreadsheet susceptible-infectious-recovered recurrence with stated contact and recovery probabilities; compare screening or prevention policies using uncertainty, privacy and distributional consequences.

practice: Evaluate a screening study and a synthetic outbreak, auditing causal claims and recommending an intervention with explicit equity tradeoffs.

includes: Oscillators, normal modes, mechanical waves, acoustics and dispersion

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Predict oscillatory and propagating physical disturbances.
decks.title: Oscillations and Waves

outcomes.description: Derive and solve damped, driven and coupled oscillator equations; calculate resonance, phase and normal modes from mechanical parameters.

Derive the one-dimensional string or acoustic wave equation from force and continuity balances, verify traveling and standing solutions and calculate impedance, reflection, dispersion and energy flux.

practice: Measure resonances in a coupled oscillator or acoustic tube and infer damping and wave speed from amplitude and phase data.

includes: Electrostatics, magnetostatics, material response and Maxwell equations

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Calculate electromagnetic fields and their physical effects.
decks.title: Electromagnetism

outcomes.description: Calculate fields and potentials from continuous charge/current distributions; apply symmetry, Gauss/Ampere laws and simple conductor/dielectric boundary conditions in three dimensions.
Use integral and differential Maxwell equations to derive induction, field energy and plane-wave propagation; calculate Lorentz-force motion and energy transfer with stated material models.

practice: Solve and compare electrostatic boundary configurations and derive a plane-wave energy balance from Maxwell equations.

excludes: General relativity and Schrödinger solution methods
includes: Special relativity and experimental origins of quantum physics

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Interpret evidence that exceeds classical mechanical models.
decks.title: Modern Physics

outcomes.description: Calculate Lorentz transformations, spacetime intervals, four-momentum conservation and relativistic collision thresholds using an explicitly defined Minkowski metric.
Analyze photoelectric, Compton, atomic-spectrum and matter-wave evidence using photon and de Broglie relations, distinguishing successful predictions from semiclassical model limitations.

practice: Reconstruct a relativistic collision and estimate physical constants from historical-style photoelectric and spectral data.

includes: Multivariate regression, generalized linear models, likelihood and model validation

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.description: Fit and validate multivariable statistical models.
decks.title: Statistical Modeling

outcomes.description: Construct Gaussian linear, logistic and Poisson models in matrix notation; derive likelihoods and gradients, fit them using a documented optimizer and interpret interactions, regularization and uncertainty.
Implement bootstrap and permutation procedures, cross-validation and multiple-testing control; diagnose leakage, misspecification, confounding and unstable coefficients.

practice: Build a reproducible regression analysis from raw data, implement resampling and defend the choice of predictive versus causal interpretation.

includes: Fourier and Laplace transforms, separation of variables and classical PDE boundary problems

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.description: Solve classical field equations in explicit coordinates.
decks.title: Transforms and Partial Differential Equations

outcomes.description: Calculate Fourier series, Fourier/Laplace transforms and convolutions; use orthogonality, eigenfunction expansions and stated convergence conditions to solve forced linear problems.

Solve heat, wave and Laplace boundary/initial-value problems in intervals, rectangles, cylinders and spheres using separation of variables, locally developed Sturm-Liouville theory and Bessel/Legendre eigenfunctions.

practice: Derive temperature and potential fields in two different geometries and check boundary conditions, dimensions and convergence of truncated expansions.

includes: Smooth and convex optimization, constrained optimality and implementable solvers

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.description: Formulate and solve continuous optimization problems.
decks.title: Continuous Optimization

outcomes.description: Establish convexity, derive first/second-order and Karush-Kuhn-Tucker conditions and use Lagrangian dual bounds under explicit constraint qualifications.
Implement gradient, Newton, projected-gradient and basic proximal methods; derive elementary convergence bounds and diagnose poor scaling and nonconvex failure.

practice: Implement constrained least-squares and sparse-estimation solvers and compare numerical stopping criteria with provable optimality certificates.

includes: Measure, Lebesgue integration, continuous probability and limit theorems

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.description: Build rigorous integration and probabilistic limit arguments.
decks.title: Measure and Probability

outcomes.description: Construct measurable functions and Lebesgue integrals and prove/apply monotone and dominated convergence, product integration and Radon-Nikodym results with explicit hypotheses.

Calculate continuous and joint distributions, conditional expectations and characteristic functions; prove core laws of large numbers and a central limit theorem and analyze elementary Markov chains and martingales.

practice: Write a measure-theoretic proof portfolio and analyze convergence of a stochastic sequence with both theorem hypotheses and counterexamples.

includes: Holomorphic functions, contour integration, residues and conformal maps

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.description: Use the rigidity of complex differentiability.
decks.title: Complex Analysis

outcomes.description: Prove and apply Cauchy-Riemann, Cauchy integral, power-series and maximum-principle results and classify isolated singularities.
Evaluate real and complex integrals with residues and branch choices; construct elementary conformal maps and use them to solve bounded two-dimensional potential problems.

practice: Produce rigorous contour calculations, including vanishing-arc estimates, and map a planar boundary problem to a solvable domain.

includes: Nonlinear dynamics, numerical time integration, feedback and deterministic state estimation

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.description: Analyze and control dynamical systems in state space.
decks.title: Dynamics and Control

outcomes.description: Analyze stability with Jacobians and Lyapunov functions, identify elementary bifurcations and implement Euler and Runge-Kutta integration with step-size and stability checks.
Construct state-space and transfer-function models, test controllability and observability, and design pole-placement feedback and Luenberger observers with robustness checks.

practice: Implement a controlled two-state plant, compare open/closed-loop behavior and demonstrate instability caused by delay or an excessive integration step.

includes: Processes, virtual memory, filesystems, concurrency and OS interfaces

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.description: Implement and reason about resource-sharing system software.
decks.title: Operating Systems

outcomes.description: Implement bounded scheduler, virtual-memory and filesystem components; explain traps, system calls, page tables, caching and crash recovery.
Use processes, threads, locks, condition variables and atomic operations through taught systems APIs; diagnose races, deadlocks and memory-ordering failures.

practice: Extend an instructional kernel and build a concurrent server, using stress tests and invariants to expose scheduling and synchronization defects.

includes: Language paradigms, parsing, type checking, intermediate representations and compilation

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.description: Translate and execute programs through explicit language representations.
decks.title: Languages and Compilers

outcomes.description: Compare imperative, functional and object-based language behavior; implement lexical analysis, recursive-descent or table-driven parsing, scope resolution and a small static type checker.
Construct an intermediate representation, implement local dataflow analysis and optimization, and generate stack-machine or assembly code with runtime storage conventions.

practice: Implement a compiler for a small typed language and test semantic preservation by differential execution against an interpreter.

includes: Threat modeling, application and network defenses, authentication and authorized assessment

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.description: Identify threats and validate proportionate defenses.
decks.title: Security Engineering

outcomes.description: Construct threat models and implement access control, input validation, secret handling and secure communication using documented cryptographic libraries and explicit trust assumptions.
Assess injection, authentication, network and memory-boundary failures in isolated examples; prioritize mitigations and justify authorization, disclosure, privacy and usability decisions.

practice: Audit a deliberately vulnerable local service, reproduce authorized failures and deliver tested repairs and a risk-based disclosure report.

includes: Supervised and unsupervised learning, neural networks, representation and evaluation

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.description: Construct predictive models and evaluate generalization.
decks.title: Machine Learning

outcomes.description: Implement linear classifiers, trees, nearest-neighbor methods, k-means, principal-component analysis and finite-mixture expectation-maximization with explicit objectives and representations.
Derive reverse-mode differentiation on computation graphs and implement a small neural network; use convolution, attention and sequence representations in documented image or text models.
Design leakage-free training and evaluation, compare calibration and subgroup errors and justify choices involving fairness, interpretability, privacy and deployment shift.

practice: Implement a baseline and neural model from explicit objectives, perform ablations and submit a reproducible model card with failure analysis.

excludes: Quantum derivation and multidimensional spin dynamics
includes: Working IR, UV-visible, first-order NMR and mass-spectral structure interpretation

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.description: Infer molecular structure from complementary spectra.
decks.title: Molecular Spectroscopy

outcomes.description: Apply explicitly taught photon-transition, harmonic-bond, shielding, first-order spin-coupling and ion-fragmentation models to predict simple spectral features and recognize their breakdown.
Combine formula, isotope patterns, IR, UV-visible and one-dimensional proton/carbon NMR evidence to distinguish constitutional and stereochemical hypotheses and identify unresolved structure.

practice: Solve blinded unknown structures and justify every assignment, including contradictory peaks and an additional experiment that would resolve ambiguity.

includes: Biomolecular chemistry, folding, enzyme models and central metabolism

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.description: Explain biological function through molecular structure and energetics.
decks.title: Biochemistry

outcomes.description: Represent proteins, nucleic acids, carbohydrates and lipids; explain folding, binding, catalysis and membrane assembly through stereochemistry, noncovalent interactions and free-energy differences.

Use a locally developed steady-state Michaelis-Menten model and inhibition variants to calculate rates; trace carbon, electrons and ATP through glycolysis, respiration, photosynthesis and biosynthetic regulation.

practice: Analyze a metabolic perturbation using molecular structures, stoichiometric balances and enzyme-rate calculations, distinguishing thermodynamic from kinetic control.

excludes: Electronic band derivations and industrial qualification
includes: Polymer synthesis classes, molecular-weight distributions and material characterization

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.description: Connect chemical structure and processing to material performance.
decks.title: Polymers and Materials

outcomes.description: Compare step-growth and chain-growth mechanisms, calculate number/weight-average molecular masses from distributions and relate architecture, crosslinking and tacticity to properties.

Interpret thermal, mechanical, chromatographic and powder-diffraction measurements using locally taught transition, stress-strain and Bragg models; compare polymers, ceramics, glasses and composites and justify lifecycle tradeoffs.

practice: Characterize a polymer or composite from supplied and measured data and recommend a material with explicit durability, recyclability and uncertainty considerations.

includes: Microbial metabolism, growth, viruses, ecology and identification

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Investigate microorganisms as organisms and interacting communities.
decks.title: Microbiology

outcomes.description: Compare bacterial, archaeal, fungal and viral replication, metabolic strategies, gene exchange and host/environment interactions; calculate growth and viable counts from dilution data.
Use culture, staining, biochemical, susceptibility and sequence-assay evidence to identify microbes and distinguish resistance, contamination, colonization and causal infection.

practice: Investigate a nonpathogenic isolate or curated case dataset with a decision tree of orthogonal tests and a contamination-control plan.

includes: Embryogenesis, patterning, differentiation, morphogenesis and regeneration

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Infer how genes and cell interactions construct organisms.
decks.title: Developmental Biology

outcomes.description: Explain axis formation, induction, morphogen thresholds, cell-fate specification and tissue movement using lineage and spatial gene-expression representations across animal and plant examples.
Interpret lineage tracing, transplantation, mosaic and loss/gain-of-function evidence; design controlled tests distinguishing cell autonomy, competence and instructive signaling.

practice: Reconstruct a developmental mechanism from spatial images and perturbations and propose a decisive lineage or rescue experiment.

includes: Innate/adaptive immunity, tolerance, vaccination and immune assays

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Explain immune responses and interpret immune evidence.
decks.title: Immunology

outcomes.description: Trace antigen recognition, presentation, lymphocyte activation, receptor diversification, effector responses, memory and tolerance and explain allergy, autoimmunity and immune evasion.
Interpret ELISA, flow-cytometry gates and vaccination data using explicitly taught assay signals, controls and denominators; distinguish immune correlates from demonstrated protection.

practice: Analyze a multigroup immune-assay dataset, construct control-aware gates and defend a limited claim about a vaccine response.

includes: Neural signaling, sensory/motor systems, plasticity and neural evidence

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Connect cellular neural signals to circuit and behavioral function.
decks.title: Neuroscience

outcomes.description: Use locally defined Nernst potentials, RC membrane response and threshold/reset models to calculate bounded neuronal responses; explain action potentials, synaptic transmission and plasticity without claiming full conductance dynamics.
Relate sensory, motor, autonomic and memory circuits to anatomy and behavior; quantify spike histograms and receptive fields and evaluate recording, lesion and intervention evidence.

practice: Analyze spike and behavioral recordings and compare a passive membrane model with observations, explicitly identifying where active-channel mechanisms are needed.

includes: Selection, drift, migration, coalescence and phylogenetic inference

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Infer evolutionary processes from genetic variation.
decks.title: Evolutionary Genetics

outcomes.description: Derive discrete allele-frequency recurrences and implement Wright-Fisher sampling, mutation, migration and selection; calculate heterozygosity, linkage disequilibrium and simple coalescent waiting probabilities.
Construct character and sequence trees using parsimony and a locally specified finite-state substitution likelihood with pruning; compare bootstrap support, homoplasy and model sensitivity.

practice: Implement a population simulator and a small-tree likelihood calculation, then compare competing historical explanations for a genetic dataset.

excludes: Wet-lab library preparation and advanced multi-omics
includes: Sequencing data models, alignment, assembly, variant analysis and genomic testing

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Reconstruct and interrogate genomes computationally.
decks.title: Genomics

outcomes.description: Explain how sequencing generates reads and quality scores; implement dynamic-programming alignment and a small de Bruijn assembly and interpret mapping, repeats and coverage limitations.

Construct a reproducible quality-control, variant and expression-count workflow using documented tools; calculate genotype likelihoods under a taught read-error model and control false discoveries in genomic comparisons.

practice: Analyze a public or synthetic read dataset with provenance and privacy controls, verifying selected calls against simulated ground truth.

includes: Population interactions, structured populations, observation models and ecological estimation

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Predict ecological dynamics and estimate hidden ecological states.
decks.title: Quantitative Ecology

outcomes.description: Construct and analyze logistic, consumer-resource, competition and age/stage-matrix models, calculating equilibria, stability, growth rates and sensitivity.

Fit abundance, occupancy and capture-recapture models using explicitly constructed detection likelihoods and documented optimizers; distinguish process/observation error and assess identifiability and out-of-sample prediction.

practice: Estimate a population trend with imperfect detection and compare competing dynamic models using held-out surveys and sensitivity analysis.

includes: Variational calculus, Lagrangian and Hamiltonian mechanics, constraints and canonical structure

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Derive dynamics from variational and geometric structure.
decks.title: Analytical Mechanics

outcomes.description: Derive Euler-Lagrange equations from the action, use generalized coordinates and constraints, and connect continuous symmetries to conserved quantities through a taught Noether argument.
Construct Hamiltonians, calculate Poisson brackets and canonical transformations and analyze rigid-body motion, small oscillations and central-force phase space.

practice: Derive a constrained multibody system in two coordinate choices and show that its conserved quantities and physical trajectories agree.

excludes: Full scattering theory and many-body approximations
includes: Wavefunctions, operators, finite-state systems, one-dimensional potentials and atomic states

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Calculate predictions from quantum states and observables.
decks.title: Quantum Mechanics

outcomes.description: Normalize complex wavefunctions, calculate continuous probability densities and expectation integrals, use bra-ket notation and Hermitian operators and evolve finite-dimensional states unitarily.

Solve one-dimensional wells, barriers and harmonic oscillators; calculate spin measurements, commutators and first-order perturbations and use supplied hydrogen eigenfunctions to interpret three-dimensional atomic quantum numbers.

practice: Calculate transmission through a one-dimensional barrier and spin-sequence probabilities, checking normalization, limiting cases and measurement interpretation.

includes: Classical ensembles, partition functions, fluctuations and transport models

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Derive macroscopic behavior from microscopic classical models.
decks.title: Statistical Mechanics

outcomes.description: Construct microcanonical and canonical ensembles, derive Boltzmann weights and partition-function relations and calculate ideal-gas, oscillator and discrete-spin thermodynamics.
Calculate fluctuations, correlations and response; derive Maxwell velocity distributions and bounded random-walk and kinetic-theory estimates for diffusion and transport.

practice: Derive thermodynamic predictions for a classical model and compare fluctuation or diffusion measurements with the model's microscopic assumptions.

includes: Instrument integration, signal extraction, parameter inference and experimental judgment

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Design and validate an integrated physical measurement.
decks.title: Experimental Physics

outcomes.description: Integrate sensors, optics, electronics and data acquisition; teach and implement discrete Fourier analysis, lock-in demodulation and noise spectra with sampling and calibration checks.

Estimate physical parameters using weighted least squares, residuals and a locally taught Jacobian covariance approximation; compare systematic-error models and justify safety, reproducibility and societal-impact decisions.

practice: Complete an optical or electromechanical measurement project with a noise budget, independent calibration, reproducible analysis and an uncertainty-supported conclusion.

includes: Observational astronomy, stellar properties, galaxies and accessible cosmological models

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Infer astronomical properties from light and motion.
decks.title: Astronomy and Astrophysics

outcomes.description: Use sky coordinates, parallax, magnitudes, flux, spectral lines, Doppler shifts and transit/light curves to infer distance, temperature, mass, radius and orbital parameters with degeneracy checks.
Apply locally taught blackbody laws, hydrostatic scaling, nuclear-energy bookkeeping and the empirical Hubble relation to explain stellar evolution, galaxies and evidence for dark components.

practice: Analyze an archival light curve and spectrum to infer a stellar or planetary system and report competing parameter explanations.

includes: Banach/Hilbert spaces, bounded operators, duality and spectral foundations

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.description: Analyze infinite-dimensional linear problems.
decks.title: Functional Analysis

outcomes.description: Prove completeness and approximation properties in sequence and function spaces; apply Hahn-Banach, uniform boundedness and open-mapping results and distinguish weak from norm convergence.
Analyze bounded and compact operators, adjoints and spectra; prove Hilbert projection and compact self-adjoint spectral results and apply variational solvability arguments.

practice: Prove solvability and stability of an infinite-dimensional variational problem and construct a counterexample when a key hypothesis fails.

includes: Smooth manifolds, tensors, differential forms, connections and curvature

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.description: Calculate and prove coordinate-independent geometric relationships.
decks.title: Differential Geometry

outcomes.description: Construct manifold charts and tangent/cotangent spaces; transform tensor components, calculate exterior derivatives and pullbacks and apply manifold Stokes' theorem.
Calculate metrics, Levi-Civita connections, geodesics and Riemann/Ricci curvature in Riemannian and Lorentzian examples and connect local curvature with geometric invariants.

practice: Calculate the same curvature invariant in two charts and derive geodesics for a curved surface and a simple Lorentzian metric.

includes: Decision and likelihood theory, asymptotic inference, hierarchical Bayes and Monte Carlo

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.description: Derive statistical guarantees and perform advanced inference.
decks.title: Graduate Statistics

outcomes.description: Analyze sufficiency, information, optimal tests and estimator risk; derive regular likelihood consistency/asymptotic normality and explain failures at boundaries or under misspecification.

Construct hierarchical Bayesian models and implement importance sampling, Metropolis-Hastings and Gibbs sampling; justify invariant distributions and diagnose convergence and posterior predictive failure.

practice: Derive an estimator's limiting law and implement a hierarchical posterior analysis, testing both interval coverage and sampling diagnostics.

includes: Modules, field extensions, Galois theory and finite-group representations

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.description: Use structural algebra to classify extensions and representations.
decks.title: Graduate Algebra

outcomes.description: Analyze modules over principal ideal domains, exact sequences and tensor products; relate module structure to canonical matrix forms and calculate finite field extensions.
Prove and apply the Galois correspondence to polynomial solvability and construct finite-group representations and character decompositions over the complex numbers.

practice: Determine a nontrivial polynomial's Galois group and decompose a finite-group action into irreducible representations with full justification.

includes: Randomized and approximation algorithms, network flow, linear programming and integer formulations

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.description: Design algorithms with stronger performance guarantees.
decks.title: Advanced Algorithms

outcomes.description: Design and prove guarantees for randomized, approximation and online algorithms using concentration bounds developed from moment and exponential arguments.
Formulate flow, linear and integer optimization models; derive linear-program duality, implement a bounded simplex solver and use relaxations, rounding and branch-and-bound with certificates or gaps.

practice: Implement an exact and an approximation approach to a resource-allocation problem and prove bounds independently of empirical benchmarks.

includes: Consistency, replication, consensus, fault tolerance and parallel computation

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.description: Construct systems that remain correct across concurrency and failures.
decks.title: Distributed and Parallel Systems

outcomes.description: Specify consistency and failure models, reason with logical clocks and implement a bounded replicated log using a taught consensus protocol; analyze partitions, recovery and impossibility assumptions.
Implement shared-memory and message-passing reductions and distributed data processing; analyze work/span, communication, load balance and reproducibility under parallel execution.

practice: Build a replicated key-value service with fault injection and a parallel data job, reporting consistency evidence and scaling bottlenecks.

includes: Operational semantics, type soundness, program logics and model checking

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.description: Prove properties of languages and programs.
decks.title: Semantics and Verification

outcomes.description: Define small- and big-step semantics and typed lambda-calculus rules; prove substitution, progress and preservation by structural induction.
Specify safety/liveness properties, derive Hoare-style proofs and weakest preconditions, and implement finite-state model checking while explaining abstraction and state-explosion limits.

practice: Prove soundness of a small language extension and verify a concurrent protocol using both a hand invariant and an implemented finite-state checker.

includes: Security games, reductions, symmetric and public-key constructions

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.description: Analyze cryptographic constructions through explicit adversarial definitions.
decks.title: Cryptography

outcomes.description: Define indistinguishability, pseudorandomness, unforgeability and computational security and construct reductions between adversarial games with quantified advantage.

Analyze encryption, authenticated encryption, signatures and key exchange based on modular arithmetic and stated hardness assumptions; separate mathematical security from randomness and side-channel failures.

practice: Write a game-based security proof and implement a toy construction solely for testing, then demonstrate why a plausible insecure variant fails.

includes: Statistical learning theory, kernels, latent-variable learning and sequential decision learning

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.description: Analyze learning guarantees and advanced representation models.
decks.title: Graduate Machine Learning

outcomes.description: Derive generalization bounds using concentration, finite classes and capacity measures; analyze regularization, kernel methods and optimization/generalization tradeoffs under explicit sampling assumptions.

Derive variational objectives for latent-variable models and implement a variational autoencoder and a finite-state reinforcement learner, teaching Bellman equations, policy gradients and off-policy evaluation assumptions.

practice: Reproduce a small learning experiment, derive its objective and test a theoretical assumption through controlled distribution shift.

includes: Robot kinematics, localization, state estimation, planning and feedback

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.description: Connect embodied sensing, inference and action.
decks.title: Robotics

outcomes.description: Construct planar and three-dimensional rigid-transform kinematics and Jacobians; derive Gaussian linear conditioning and implement Kalman/extended-Kalman localization with sensor and linearization models.
Implement configuration-space collision checking, graph/sampling-based path planning and trajectory feedback; validate estimation consistency, constraints and human-safety failure cases.

practice: Implement a mobile-robot localization and navigation pipeline in simulation and test sensor dropout, obstacle uncertainty and controller failure.

includes: Chemical potentials, nonideal mixtures, phase equilibria and thermodynamic response

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.description: Derive equilibrium and stability in chemical systems.
decks.title: Chemical Thermodynamics

outcomes.description: Derive thermodynamic potentials, Maxwell relations, chemical potentials and partial molar quantities; calculate activities and fugacities using specified nonideal models.
Determine reaction and multicomponent phase equilibria, construct phase diagrams and apply Gibbs phase rule and stability criteria with explicit standard-state conventions.

practice: Construct a binary-mixture phase diagram from a free-energy model and infer nonideality parameters from phase-equilibrium data using a provided solver.

includes: Molecular orbitals, symmetry, bonding and quantum spectroscopy

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.description: Connect quantum states to molecular bonding and spectra.
decks.title: Quantum Chemistry

outcomes.description: Construct Born-Oppenheimer molecular Hamiltonians and linear-combination orbital models; use locally taught point-group operations and character tables to form symmetry-adapted orbitals and calculate simple secular energies.

Derive rigid-rotor and harmonic vibrational spectra and dipole selection rules; calculate rotational/vibrational constants and interpret electronic transitions and ligand-field bonding beyond qualitative models.

practice: Build a small molecular-orbital secular calculation and infer bond length and force constant from rotational-vibrational data.

includes: Replication, repair, expression, chromatin and molecular genetic intervention

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Explain and experimentally interrogate gene expression and genome maintenance.
decks.title: Molecular Genetics

outcomes.description: Trace replication, repair, recombination, transcription, RNA processing, translation and chromatin regulation; predict molecular consequences of sequence and regulatory perturbations.

Design cloning, reporter, quantitative-PCR, genome-editing and rescue experiments using explicit construct maps, guide/primer constraints and controls; distinguish off-target, dosage and regulatory effects.

practice: Design and, where authorized, execute a benign reporter perturbation with sequence-verified constructs, normalized measurements and a rescue test.

includes: Green functions, multipoles, waveguides, radiation and covariant electrodynamics

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Solve advanced classical electromagnetic field problems.
decks.title: Graduate Electrodynamics

outcomes.description: Construct electrostatic Green functions and multipole expansions, solve cylindrical/spherical boundary problems and derive guided-wave and dielectric-interface modes.
Derive retarded potentials and dipole radiation, calculate angular power patterns and express Maxwell equations and field transformations in covariant tensor notation taught locally.

practice: Derive a waveguide mode and a radiating-source field, verifying boundary conditions, gauge consistency and energy conservation.

includes: Approximation methods, angular momentum, scattering, density matrices and identical particles

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Solve quantum problems beyond exactly soluble introductory models.
decks.title: Graduate Quantum Mechanics

outcomes.description: Derive variational, WKB, degenerate and time-dependent perturbation methods; combine angular momenta and derive central-potential radial solutions using a locally developed Frobenius procedure.
Calculate Born and partial-wave scattering, construct bosonic/fermionic many-particle states and density matrices and analyze reduced states, entanglement and measurement statistics.

practice: Compare variational and numerical bound-state estimates and calculate a scattering observable, including approximation-validity checks.

includes: Grand ensembles, quantum gases, interacting models and phase transitions

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Analyze quantum populations and collective thermal behavior.
decks.title: Quantum Statistical Physics

outcomes.description: Derive grand-canonical Bose and Fermi occupations from state counting; calculate blackbody, degenerate-gas and Bose-condensation observables and thermodynamic limits.
Derive mean-field and Landau descriptions of ordering, analyze correlations and critical scaling and implement Metropolis sampling with detailed-balance and finite-size checks.

practice: Compare a simulated spin-model transition with mean-field predictions and calculate a quantum-gas thermodynamic curve with numerical error control.

excludes: Field-theoretic scattering derivations and radiation-handling credentials
includes: Nuclear structure, decay, reactions, particle classification and detector evidence

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Connect subatomic models to reaction and detector observations.
decks.title: Nuclear and Particle Physics

outcomes.description: Calculate binding energies, decay chains, tunneling estimates and reaction Q-values using liquid-drop, shell and barrier models; distinguish fission, fusion and decay mechanisms.

Apply conservation laws, relativistic invariant masses and cross-section definitions to particle reactions; interpret tracking, calorimetry and counting data using locally taught efficiency, Poisson-count and background models.

practice: Reconstruct a resonance from simulated detector events and audit energy thresholds, detector efficiency and alternative background explanations.

includes: Crystals, bands, phonons, transport, magnetism and soft/ordered matter

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Predict material behavior from microscopic structure.
decks.title: Condensed Matter Physics

outcomes.description: Construct reciprocal lattices and Brillouin zones, derive one-dimensional nearly-free-electron and tight-binding bands and use locally specified Fermi occupation and density-of-states models for metals and semiconductors.

Calculate lattice normal modes, thermal capacities and Drude transport; analyze bounded spin, elastic and polymer-chain models and interpret evidence for magnetic, liquid-crystalline and superconducting order.

practice: Derive a lattice dispersion and infer material parameters from diffraction, heat-capacity and conductivity datasets, identifying model failures.

includes: Einstein equations, relativistic matter, Schwarzschild geometry and gravitational waves

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Calculate gravitational phenomena as spacetime dynamics.
decks.title: General Relativity

outcomes.description: Construct stress-energy tensors for particles and perfect fluids, derive geodesic motion variationally and apply Einstein equations and covariant conservation to symmetric metrics.
Calculate Schwarzschild redshift, orbit precession, light deflection and horizon properties and derive linearized gravitational-wave propagation and detector strain.

practice: Derive and compare two observable relativistic corrections and calculate curvature and causal behavior near a Schwarzschild horizon.

includes: Stellar structure, radiative transfer, compact objects and quantitative cosmology

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Build quantitative models of stars and cosmic expansion.
decks.title: Stellar and Cosmological Physics

outcomes.description: Derive and numerically integrate spherical stellar mass, pressure, luminosity and temperature equations using stated opacity and nuclear-rate models; solve one-dimensional radiative transfer and analyze degenerate support.

Use explicitly stated Friedmann equations and matter/radiation equations of state to calculate expansion histories, distances and horizons; fit bounded cosmological models and assess parameter degeneracies without claiming an Einstein-equation derivation.

practice: Implement a stellar-structure shooting calculation and compare expansion-distance predictions with an archival dataset using a supplied least-squares tool.

includes: Weak derivatives, Sobolev spaces, energy estimates and finite-difference/finite-element methods

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.description: Establish and approximate solutions of field equations.
decks.title: Advanced PDE Methods

outcomes.description: Define distributions, weak derivatives and Sobolev spaces; derive weak formulations and energy estimates and prove representative elliptic existence/uniqueness and parabolic stability results.

Implement finite differences for one- and two-dimensional diffusion/waves and piecewise-linear finite elements for elliptic equations on triangular meshes; analyze consistency, stability, convergence and mesh error.

practice: Prove an energy estimate and implement two discretizations with manufactured solutions, mesh refinement and a demonstrated unstable parameter choice.

includes: Electrode kinetics, diffusion, interfacial charge and electrochemical inverse methods

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.description: Connect electrochemical signals to transport and interfacial mechanisms.
decks.title: Electrochemistry and Interfaces

outcomes.description: Derive bounded Butler-Volmer/Tafel, diffusion-layer and double-layer equivalent-circuit models with stated assumptions; calculate current, overpotential, limiting flux and charging transients.
Interpret voltammetry and impedance data using documented fitting tools, distinguish kinetic, transport and capacitive effects and evaluate corrosion, battery or electrocatalytic design tradeoffs.

practice: Analyze a supervised cell or archived electrochemical dataset and distinguish multiple mechanisms through perturbation and residual analysis.

includes: Stereoselective synthesis, pericyclic reactions, catalytic transformations and route validation

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.description: Design and substantiate multistep molecular syntheses.
decks.title: Advanced Synthesis

outcomes.description: Plan convergent multistep routes using stereoselective carbon-carbon construction, locally taught frontier-orbital/pericyclic selection rules and organocatalytic or metal-catalyzed transformations.

Compare mechanistic and spectral evidence for product identity and selectivity; optimize a bounded synthesis using controls, mass balance and kinetic evidence and justify safety and sustainability tradeoffs.

practice: Defend two competing routes to a complex target and execute or critically reconstruct a supervised short sequence with identity, purity and waste evidence.

excludes: Every homogeneous and heterogeneous catalyst class
includes: Organometallic bonding, catalytic cycles, inorganic mechanisms and spectroscopic discrimination

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.description: Explain and test inorganic catalytic mechanisms.
decks.title: Inorganic Chemistry and Catalysis

outcomes.description: Construct orbital and electron-count descriptions of metal-ligand bonding and predict oxidative addition, reductive elimination, insertion, elimination and ligand-exchange pathways.
Derive catalytic rate/selectivity models and distinguish resting states and turnover-limiting steps using kinetic, isotope, spectroscopic and poisoning evidence for molecular and surface catalysts.

practice: Construct competing catalytic cycles and design a minimal set of kinetic and spectroscopic experiments that discriminates between them.

includes: Hartree-Fock, density-functional models, correlation, potential-energy surfaces and validation

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.description: Calculate molecular electronic structure with controlled approximations.
decks.title: Electronic Structure Methods

outcomes.description: Derive Slater-determinant Hartree-Fock and generalized self-consistent-field equations and implement a small restricted solver using supplied integrals; explain density-functional and perturbative/configuration-interaction correlation approximations.

Use documented electronic-structure tools for geometries, frequencies and reaction paths; distinguish basis, correlation, functional, spin and convergence errors and validate energies and spectra against independent evidence.

practice: Implement minimal-basis Hartree-Fock and benchmark a reaction-energy prediction across documented approximation levels without treating software agreement as proof.

includes: Molecular dynamics, Monte Carlo, molecular force fields and free-energy estimation

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.description: Sample molecular systems and infer equilibrium properties.
decks.title: Molecular Simulation

outcomes.description: Implement pair forces, periodic boundaries, neighbor lists, velocity-Verlet integration and Metropolis moves; compare ensembles, thermostats, conservation, equilibration and autocorrelation using explicit molecular-coordinate models.

Derive free-energy perturbation and umbrella-reweighting estimators, use documented sampling tools and quantify overlap, finite-size, sampling and force-field uncertainties against independent structural or thermodynamic data.

practice: Implement a simple molecular fluid and estimate a free-energy difference with replicate trajectories, overlap diagnostics and a force-field sensitivity study.

includes: Quantitative imaging, signaling dynamics, cell-fate research and causal perturbations

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Design mechanistic cellular and developmental investigations.
decks.title: Cellular and Developmental Research

outcomes.description: Use documented segmentation and tracking tools after teaching thresholding, connected components and assignment procedures; quantify cell trajectories, localization and lineage transitions with artifact and uncertainty checks.

Integrate timed genetic perturbations, rescue, live imaging and molecular readouts to discriminate signaling, mechanical and cell-fate mechanisms; justify model-organism choice and welfare or consent tradeoffs.

practice: Reanalyze a live-cell dataset and propose a factorial perturbation study with quantified competing predictions, negative controls and a reproducible image-analysis audit.

includes: Biochemical networks, metabolic flux, dynamic regulation and system identification

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Construct and test mechanistic models of biological networks.
decks.title: Systems Biology

outcomes.description: Construct stoichiometric matrices and mass-action/enzyme-rate ODEs for metabolism and gene regulation; analyze conservation, steady flux null spaces, feedback, bistability and oscillation.

Estimate dynamic parameters using documented optimizers, implement sensitivity equations and profile-likelihood checks and design perturbations that distinguish structurally or practically unidentifiable models.

practice: Implement a regulatory-network ODE model, fit a perturbation time course and propose a new measurement that resolves a demonstrated parameter ambiguity.

excludes: Every omics technology and de novo protein-folding algorithm
includes: Single-cell and multi-omics inference, sequence models, structural interpretation and validation

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Infer biological structure and function from high-dimensional molecular evidence.
decks.title: Advanced Bioinformatics

outcomes.description: Construct count-based and latent-variable models for bulk/single-cell molecular data, account for batch and missingness and integrate expression, accessibility and sequence evidence without conflating clusters with cell identities.

Implement a sequence hidden-Markov model with forward/backward inference; use documented protein-structure and interaction tools with confidence/coordinate interpretation and validate functional hypotheses against independent experiments and leakage-aware benchmarks.

practice: Complete a multi-omics reanalysis and a sequence-model implementation, separating computational confidence from experimental validation of biological mechanism.

includes: Conductance models, neural networks, spike-process models and neural coding

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Model neural dynamics and infer neural representations.
decks.title: Computational Neuroscience

outcomes.description: Derive conductance-based membrane and gating equations, implement single-neuron and coupled excitatory/inhibitory networks and analyze equilibria, excitability, oscillations and explicit plasticity rules.

Derive a conditional-intensity point-process likelihood from time-bin probabilities, fit encoding/decoding models and compare information measures and held-out predictions under stimulus and intervention controls.

practice: Implement a conductance-based circuit and fit a spike-encoding model, comparing dynamical mechanism, predictive fit and intervention evidence.

excludes: All spatial stochastic-process and diffusion-limit theories
includes: Eco-evolutionary feedback, spatial discrete models, hierarchical field inference and research design

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Connect ecological and evolutionary theory to imperfect field evidence.
decks.title: Ecological and Evolutionary Research

outcomes.description: Derive invasion-fitness and coupled trait/population models and implement spatial patch and individual-based stochastic models; compare deterministic and stochastic predictions and assess scale dependence.

Construct hierarchical models integrating demographic, environmental and genetic observations; evaluate posterior predictive adequacy and design monitoring or experiments that distinguish eco-evolutionary mechanisms.

practice: Fit an integrated population model, compare competing spatial or evolutionary mechanisms and defend a feasible, ethically justified field-research design.

scopeIssues: Physics: established working fluid mechanics and its advanced continuum continuation remain unfinished. Pressure, flow and diffusion applications appear in physical foundations, physiology, waves and statistical mechanics, but no contract teaches deriving and solving viscous incompressible flow or validating a fluid experiment. These neighboring outcomes do not provide full undergraduate-advanced fluid-mechanics coverage.

Physics: established plasma-physics foundations remain unfinished. Electromagnetism and statistical mechanics do not teach charged-fluid or kinetic plasma models, Debye screening, plasma oscillations and magnetized transport as a coherent graduate capability.

Chemistry: established graduate molecular spectroscopy remains unfinished. The included chemistry/molecular-spectroscopy outcomes provide working first-order interpretation and chemistry/quantum-chemistry provides basic quantum spectra, but no contract teaches multidimensional NMR pulse-sequence reasoning or time-resolved molecular spectroscopic inference at graduate depth.

Mathematics: linear programming has a teaching contract in computer-science/advanced-algorithms, but its only route imposes the complete advanced-algorithm curriculum rather than an independent undergraduate working entry. An accessible linear/discrete optimization route remains to be separated while preserving the graduate guarantees.
